Image Processing and Learning-based Techniques for Nuclei-Centric Studies in Digital Histopathology

Abstract:

Histopathological examination plays an important role in cancer diagnosis and grading through the assessment of tissue architecture, cellular composition, nuclear morphology, and mitotic activity. However, manual examination of large volumes of biopsy samples and complex tissue regions is time-consuming, depends on the expertise of pathologists, and is sometimes affected by inter- and intra-observer variability. Computer-assisted analysis supports pathologists by providing quantitative information on cellular and nuclear characteristics, as well as reducing the burden of repetitive visual evaluation. Variations in the appearance of nuclei in different organs, patient populations, staining conditions, and imaging settings make automatic analysis more challenging. Nuclei also show considerable variation in size, shape, orientation, texture, and spatial organization as touching or densely clustered structures. In addressing these challenges, the
proposed research will investigate image-processing and learning-based techniques for nuclei-centric analysis of H&ampE-stained histopathological images of multiple organs. The work will focus on accurate nuclei segmentation to obtain reliable individual nuclear regions for improved analysis and characterization. Simultaneous classification of cell types will help pathologists to obtain relevant information on cellular composition of the tissue. It is pertinent to mention that histopathological analysis is not only critical for diagnosis but also for grading the severity of the cancer through the detection of mitotic figures. The development of an accurate mitotic detection algorithm will lead to an improved diagnosis and early grading of cancer. To make this study more generalized and robust, variations in organ type, demographic background, staining appearance, and imaging conditions will be incorporated during the development of the algorithms. The expected outcome of the research is an integrated AI-assisted framework for nuclei-centric analysis of multi-organ histopathological images. The framework is intended to provide pathologists with consistent and quantitative nuclei-level information, assist in the assessment of diagnostically relevant cellular characteristics, and reduce repetitive manual analysis. The proposed research is expected to contribute to reliable quantitative nuclei-centric analysis in digital histopathology, assist pathologists in cancer diagnosis and provide a second opinion for further decision-making.
